Division Management Award -
Don Mooney
The Division Management Award is
given to recognize the one manage-
ment employee who most closely
works through team effort towards
achievement of our mission and
goals. The winner of the Division
Management Award for 1987 is Don
Mooney, Supervisor of JFK Inflight
Services.
Don Mooney thought that he was
attending the Jan. 26 awards dinner
as the recipient of an Outstanding
Contributions Award. Instead,
Mooney was surprised at the cere-
mony to find that he had also won the
division top management award for
his work on the establishment of JFK
as an International base in 1987. Paul
Green said of him, "Starting a new
domicile entails a myriad of items that
need to be accomplished and a lot of
brainstorming to anticipate the unex-
pected. At a small domicile location,
they rely exclusively on the existing
staff to pick up new assignments and
use their creativity and initiative to
make it work. Don did all of this and
more. It should be mentioned that he
approached all of these challenges
with enthusiasm. Don's challenges
included: coordinating orientation
and training for 80 international flight
attendants; becoming an expert on
the 747-200; establishing excellent
working relationships with LAXSK,
their new International Service Cen-
ter, and local maintenance, station
operations, ramp services and food
the unit has excellent productivity
and produces an outstanding prod-
uct. We depend on his expertise to
aid us in doing business in the Ori-
ent. He is required to coordinate our
facility, equipment and inventory
management, personnel relations
and resolve any other challenges that
may arise and make it all work,
Orient-style, to United's advantage.
Ed Kobayashi is one of the most en-
thusiastic, energetic, dedicated em-
ployees I have had the pleasure to
associate with in many years. Ed is
truly an asset to our Food Services
division," concluded O'Brien.
• John Corpening, ORDSW
• Kate Mc Namara, SFOSW
service team members to ensure a
successful operation. Don's dedica-
tion and 'can-do' spirit never seems
to end. He has sacrificed personal
plans several times when, at the last
moment, he was called upon to fly to
Japan to avoid flight cancellations,"
Green commented.
Photos of these award winners are
in this issue of INFLIGHT. Photos of
the Pacific Division winners were not
available in time for this issue. They
will be highlighted next month.
• Flight Attendants of the Year for Customer Interaction are: (Front Row) Thomas Le Penske, SEASW; Sikoki Layton, LAXSW; Kate Mc Namara, SFOSW; Brenda Mahoney,
DENSW; John Corpening, ORDSW. (Back Row): Lorenzo Morejon, JFKSW: Richard Vogt, EWRSW; Judy Lee, DCASW; Mark Kaplan, HNLSW; Michael Mate, CLESW.
Photo by Ken Goetz, EXOAL.
Customer Interaction
here are 13,000 flight attend-
ants eligible to be nominated
as domicile flight attendant of
the year for Customer Interaction, but
only ten can win this award. So the
ten winners you see on this page
represent the very highest achieve-
ment in onboard performance and
Customer Interaction. This award
recognizes flight attendants who
consistently display an ability and
commitment to cause customers to
fly United Airlines again. These win-
ners also set good examples for fly-
ing partners and demonstrate an
unwavering commitment to the flight
attendant profession.
Some of our Flight Attendants of
the Year have as little as one year of
seniority, and some have more than
20. But, whatever their tenure, they
all share certain traits - enthusiasm,
a willingness to step forward and lend
a helping hand, and superior people
skills.
Ron Tokuyama,
Inflight Services Director, Domestic
